title: Chicken Shawarma
subtitle: Middle Eastern spiced chicken with garlic sauce
excerpt: Chicken thighs marinated in a warm spice blend of cumin, turmeric, cinnamon, and paprika, then roasted at high heat until caramelised, and served in flatbread with garlic sauce, pickled chilli, and herbs.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shawarma is a method of cooking meat in which cuts are stacked on a vertical rotisserie spit and slowly rotated while cooking, the outer layers being shaved off as they cook. The technique originated in Ottoman Turkey (doner kebab), with the Middle Eastern version using different spicing and serving style. The word shawarma comes from the Turkish çevirme, meaning 'turning'. Restaurant shawarma is cooked on the spit for many hours; the home version replicates the flavour profile by marinating thinly sliced or boneless thigh meat in the shawarma spice blend and roasting at high heat to get caramelisation.

content.text: Boneless, skin-on thighs work best here: they stay moist during high-heat roasting and develop the caramelisation you need. Marinate overnight if you can. The garlic sauce (toum) is the essential accompaniment: a stable emulsion of garlic, lemon juice, and oil that is intensely garlicky and creamy. If you do not have time to make toum, garlic-heavy mayonnaise is an acceptable substitute.

Combine the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, turmeric, paprika, cinnamon, allspice, coriander, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Add the chicken thighs and turn to coat thoroughly. Marinate for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight in the fridge.

Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Spread the chicken in a single layer in a roasting tin. Roast for 30 to 35 minutes until the chicken is deeply coloured and caramelised at the edges, and cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes, then slice the chicken across the grain into strips. Serve in warm flatbreads with sliced tomato, parsley, pickled chilli, and garlic sauce or hummus.
